title: Finiteness of the Regularized Prime Sine Series
content: A rigorous finite meaning to the divergent prime sine sum \( \sum_p p^{-\sigma}\sin(T\log p),\qquad \frac12<\sigma<1, \) is formulated by defining its canonical regularization through the analytic continuation of the prime zeta function. Proving unconditionally that the regularized sum is locally bounded and harmonic on the entire strip, except at a discrete exceptional set corresponding to nontrivial zeros of \( \zeta \) with real part in \( (\frac12,1) \). At a zero of multiplicity \( r \), the regularized sum has finite one-sided limits and a jump of \( -r\pi \) in the \( T \)-variable; everywhere else it is real analytic. The \( m=1 \) prime term is the sole carrier of the jumps; the \( m=2 \) and \( m\ge3 \) prime-power terms are smooth at positive zero ordinates. The exceptional set has zero density by Ingham’s unconditional estimate. At the boundary \( \sigma=\frac12 \), the standard jump measure \( -\pi\sum_{\gamma>0}M(\gamma)\delta_\gamma \) is recovered. This provides a precise, unconditional description of how the zeros of \( \zeta \) in the critical strip appear as jump singularities of a single analytically continued arithmetic function.
